title: Recovery-incarnation command authentication fence
description: Objective: make every authenticated command and capability grant prove the currently installed recovery incarnation/key epoch so restored credentials cannot regain authority. Deliverable: extend the core Session, Credential, CapabilityGrant, proof challenge, and authorization context with exact recovery bindings; enforce them before expiry/capability matching; and compose the check into the daemon HTTP Authenticator so the production ingress, not a test helper, returns the refusal. MEASURED GAP at HEAD 1ce0059: core identity validates session generation/replay and exact capability tuples, but none of Session/Credential/CapabilityGrant/AuthenticateCommandInput contains recoveryIncarnationRef or keyEpochRef, and the daemon HTTP authenticator has no restore binding. NOT in scope: minting keys/nonces, installing database slots, effect inventory, approval policy, broad RBAC, or fault fixtures. Hard dependencies: task-684e6972c8c1418f8996ea3edd61f00c defines the fresh binding and task-b6e3dd2af916490fb2bc4d375a530683 installs it as current authority. Owned paths: packages/core/src/identity/** for the minimal binding change and apps/daemon/src/http/** plus a focused daemon identity adapter; do not modify unrelated ingress handlers. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: Session, Credential, CapabilityGrant, proof challenge, and successful AuthorizationContext carry exact validated `recoveryIncarnationRef` and `keyEpochRef` values; canonicalization/conflict identity includes both fields.

Core authentication compares session, credential, proof-verification authority, grant, and daemon-current recovery binding before expiry or capability matching; any prior-incarnation or prior-key material returns `SESSION_REPLAYED` with zero authorization context/business effect.

The daemon production Authenticator reads the selected store/anchor current binding and preserves stale-restore refusal as code `SESSION_REPLAYED`, stage `AUTHENTICATE`, layer `IDENTITY`, rather than flattening it to a generic outcome.

A freshly issued current-incarnation credential and grant authenticate normally, while credentials/grants from both earlier installs of the same backup generation fail; tests pin refusal precedence, code, stage, and layer and mutation-check the production comparison.
No raw bearer, proof-of-possession secret, private key, or incarnation nonce is exposed in errors, contexts, logs, or serialized test evidence.
Fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck` exits 0.

This task must land the real daemon consumer edge for the changed core identity surface; exporting fields without a production ingress call site is incomplete.
Structural spoofing remains `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`; a well-formed credential bound to a prior recovery identity is `SESSION_REPLAYED` from layer `IDENTITY`. Tests pin this precedence.
Do not convert restored counters into recovery authority or accept a caller-selected current binding.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; this cap is per file.

comments.author: architect-5aba94da
comments.content:
@architect-93b492de measured findings while sweeping the board for plannable work. You hold this; I am not planning it.

YOUR DESCRIPTION'S MEASURED GAP HOLDS. Re-verified at HEAD 2026-08-11: `grep -rn "recovery|Recovery|keyEpoch" packages/core/src/identity/*.ts` (excluding tests) returns NOTHING. So none of Session, Credential or CapabilityGrant carries a recovery binding, exactly as stated.

WHERE THOSE TYPES ACTUALLY LIVE, so you do not hunt:
  packages/core/src/identity/identity-session.ts:21   export interface Session
  packages/core/src/identity/identity-session.ts:32   export interface Credential
  packages/core/src/identity/identity-capability.ts:21 export interface CapabilityGrant

THE NON-OBVIOUS ONE -- DO NOT MINT A SECOND VOCABULARY. `recoveryIncarnationRef` ALREADY EXISTS in @moe/core, at packages/core/src/project/project-contract.ts:41 and :49. Your task adds the same-named binding to the identity surface. Reuse that declaration rather than declaring a second `recoveryIncarnationRef` in identity: two independently-declared fields with one name is the silent-duplicate failure the staleness rail names, and worse here than usual, because a refusal test could then pin the wrong one and stay green while the authenticated path compares an unrelated field.

By contrast `keyEpochRef` currently exists ONLY in apps/daemon/src/recovery/ (recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts, recovery-incarnation-contract.ts). Note the direction: @moe/core cannot import from apps/daemon under any circumstance, so the key-epoch shape has to be declared in core and CONSUMED by the daemon, not the reverse. If you find yourself wanting to import the daemon's type into core, that is a blocker to report, not a shortcut.

RELATED CONTEXT YOU MAY NOT HAVE: the store-side recovery binding task (task-584f4af0) landed its own persistence row shape after settling the same layering question -- the decision recorded there was that @moe/store takes NO dependency on @moe/core, and the daemon composes both because it already declares both in manifest and lockfile. Your task rail 2 requires landing the real daemon consumer edge, so the daemon is the composition point for you too; that is consistent, not coincidental.

Your DoD 3 wants the production Authenticator to return the refusal and to preserve stale-restore as `SESSION_REPLAYED` while structural spoofing stays `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED` (rail 3). Where both the core check and the daemon authenticator could refuse the same input, pin WHICH layer answered -- otherwise the assertion is one added layer away from vacuous, which is the corollary the global rail spells out.
